transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net broadband advanced technical support, my name is Fiona. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Fiona, my name is Yasmin Patel. We live adjacent to a commercial light-industrial estate in Birmingham, and every morning at eight o'clock when the workshops power up their machinery, our home Wi-Fi network completely collapses across both 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands, dropping our connections and making remote work impossible!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good afternoon Yasmin. If I understand correctly, your home Wi-Fi network experiences catastrophic interference and connection collapse across both 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz radio bands every morning at eight o'clock coinciding with neighboring industrial machinery powering up. Before we examine your hub's RF spectrum analyzer telemetry, could you please confirm your full postal address and your account security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it is 19 Forge Lane, Birmingham, B12 0JJ, security PIN 7192, router model S-Net Hub 5.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Yasmin, that confirms your account details. Have you noticed whether devices connected via Ethernet cable maintain internet connectivity during the Wi-Fi drop?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, our desktop computer connected via Ethernet cable stays online at 500 Mbps, but every smartphone, tablet, and wireless laptop in the house drops off Wi-Fi completely.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Could I place you on hold for two minutes while I query your Hub 5 real-time wireless channel noise floor and non-Wi-Fi RF energy telemetry?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for holding, Yasmin. Looking at the RF spectrum analyzer telemetry, your Hub 5 is detecting massive radio frequency interference with a noise floor of minus 62 dBm across standard UNII-1 wireless channels 36 to 48.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What would cause a minus 62 dBm noise floor on channels 36 to 48?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Heavy electromagnetic pulse radiation from high-frequency industrial arc welding or motor drives radiates broad-spectrum noise that blinds the hub's standard receiver channels.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can we move our Wi-Fi to frequencies outside the welding interference?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, we can migrate your Hub 5 to protected Dynamic Frequency Selection channels in the upper UNII-2 Extended band between channels 100 and 128.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Do the industrial welding machines reach into channels 100 to 128?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No, the DFS frequency block operates at higher carrier frequencies completely isolated from industrial electromagnetic induction harmonics.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That sounds like the perfect technical solution.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am locking your Hub 5 5 GHz radio to DFS Channel 104 with 80 MHz channel width.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously high-frequency industrial induction requires advanced channel allocation rather than standard factory auto-tuning.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I understand specialized channel tuning is essential near factories.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am pushing the DFS channel assignment payload directly to your router.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The hub's center light flashed amber for three seconds and returned to solid white.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yasmin speaking, I am a pediatric cardiology nurse practitioner, and this morning at ten o'clock I am running a critical remote telemetry clinic monitoring eighteen vulnerable infants recovering at home from neonatal heart surgery! If my Wi-Fi drops while I am reviewing these infants' cardiac arrhythmias, a baby could enter cardiac arrest without warning and die before an ambulance is dispatched! I am terrified and shaking with anxiety!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am querying the RF spectrum analyzer telemetry on your Hub 5 right now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Please do Fiona, I am desperate to reach my infant patients before ten o'clock.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand the acute terror, shaking anxiety, and profound responsibility you are bearing, Yasmin, especially with eighteen vulnerable infants recovering from neonatal heart surgery relying on your remote cardiac monitoring today. While our carrier policy cannot dispatch an emergency field technician within one hour to investigate external industrial factories, I will stay on the line with you right now and personally verify that your wireless devices connect to the new DFS channels with zero packet drop.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Fiona! Let us test connecting our wireless devices right now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: On your smartphone or laptop, open your Wi-Fi settings and ensure you are connected to your S-Net network.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Checking Wi-Fi settings... Connected to 'S-Net Hub 5 5G'... Signal bars are full!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now run a live wireless speed and ping jitter test while I monitor the RF spectrum noise floor on our console.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Running speed test on laptop over Wi-Fi... Fiona! Download speed is 490 Mbps, upload is 52 Mbps, ping latency is 8 milliseconds with 0% packet loss! The connection is lightning fast!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Looking at our console, the noise floor on Channel 104 is an ultra-clean minus 94 dBm with zero interference from the industrial workshops.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Minus 94 dBm! That is pristine!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That confirms your remote cardiac telemetry session will operate with absolute stability.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: All eighteen infants will receive safe and uninterrupted cardiac monitoring today.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have locked Channel 104 permanently into your hub cloud profile so the automated night-time channel hopper never reverts to standard channels.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That will protect my clinical clinic every single morning.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have documented the industrial RF mitigation under ticket reference RF-DFS-88192-B.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: RF-DFS-88192-B, recorded in my medical clinic book.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have also scheduled our network automation to poll your hub's noise floor at eight o'clock tomorrow morning to confirm ongoing clearance.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Fiona, that automated morning check is wonderful reassurance.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please give my heartfelt best wishes to the infants and families in your care today, Yasmin.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You have brought immense peace of mind to our hospital team today.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It is our absolute honor to support your vital pediatric nursing work.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I can now log into the cardiac telemetry server with complete confidence.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before we conclude, what was that Birmingham postal address again?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: As I told you right at the start of our call, it is 19 Forge Lane, Birmingham.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Yasmin, address confirmed on the monitoring ticket.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you again Fiona for your compassionate and urgent help.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It has been an absolute pleasure assisting you, Yasmin. Have a wonderful and successful clinic.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye Fiona.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there any other technical issue I can assist with today, Yasmin?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No Fiona, everything is working flawlessly.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net broadband advanced technical support, Yasmin. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye Fiona.

transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net. Goodbye.
